measured_on.method: Every rung re-run at all 21 rebalance anchors (every=21). The figures below are the ANCHOR MEDIAN with the full range shown. A single anchor is luck: the first ladder drafted for this feature quoted a -25.4% drawdown that turned out to be the best of 21 phases, with a median of -29.2%.
measured_on.caveat: These are IN-SAMPLE dev-window figures, not out-of-sample. quantfirm/equities/backtest.py:walk_forward fits no parameters on its in-sample folds, so its output is arithmetically identical to a single run over the same bars — the 'OOS' in oos_sharpe is a misnomer this repo inherited and has not yet fixed. Stock-track rungs additionally carry survivorship bias (the 200-name universe was chosen with hindsight); the firm's standing policy is a 0.70 haircut on stock-track Sharpe, applied in the sharpe_haircut field. Only 'balanced' has ever been run on the sealed holdout.

disclosure: None of these profiles contains a working in-strategy drawdown defense.

xsec_refined documents a per-name absolute-momentum filter that routes failing slots into defensive ETFs. It never fires. Measured directly: 0 rejections across 89 dev rebalance dates at every top_n from 3 to 12, and setting abs_filter=false produces bit-identical weight matrices (DataFrame.equals() == True). The binding condition is that fewer than band_mult*top_n of ~193 names have positive 8-month momentum — 9.3% breadth at top_n=6, against a dev floor of 16.6%. That is a structural property of ranking by momentum/vol, not a quirk of this sample.

The signal also excludes the most recent ~21 trading days by construction (skip=21), so even if it did fire it would fire late. At the 2020-03-04 rebalance, three weeks into the COVID crash, it did not.
For the two stock rungs the kill switch IS the risk control. There is nothing between a drawdown and the halt line.

The choice between 'balanced' and 'aggressive' is not statistically resolvable on this data. Their Sharpes are identical to three decimals and their return streams correlate 0.947; a Jobson-Korkie test on the pair returns z = 0.00. Treat it as a concentration preference, not a performance upgrade.

The published figures are UNCAPPED backtests; the live planner enforces max_single_name_frac and redistributes the excess. Over the same dev window the cap binds on 2.2% of rebalances for balanced and aggressive and 0% for conservative, and the effect is immaterial — re-measuring balanced with the cap applied gives Sharpe 1.348 against 1.349 uncapped, drawdown unchanged. (Over the longer panel including the live period it binds more often — 8.5% balanced, 4.2% aggressive — because inverse-vol weighting concentrates harder in recent low-dispersion ranks; see IDEA_BACKLOG L.1.)

balanced's -50% halt line is only 1.31x its worst measured drawdown (-38.3%) and 1.28x its actual holdout drawdown (-39%). That is thin, and it is a deliberate pre-existing owner choice, not a recommendation. conservative sits at 1.94x and aggressive at 1.51x.

If the kill switch trips, recovery is deliberate, not automatic: `python scripts/equity_rebalance.py resume --i-accept`. Deleting the state/KILL_SWITCH_EQ file by hand does NOT work — peak_equity does not decay, so the next plan re-trips it immediately.

Halt-line headroom across the ladder (kill / worst measured anchor): conservative 1.94x, balanced 1.31x, aggressive 1.51x, ultra_aggressive 1.54x. Higher rungs do not get a tighter halt — a tight line on a violent book converts a survivable drawdown into a permanent exit. It means the opposite of safety.

ETF exposure is explicit per rung (`holds_etfs`). balanced, aggressive and ultra_aggressive hold single-name stocks only — verified max ETF weight 0.0000 across the whole dev window. conservative is entirely ETFs by design.

conservative.headline: Trend-following ETF book. Roughly half the drawdown, roughly a sixth of the return.

measured.holdout: not measured — the sealed holdout is deliberately not re-opened per profile

conservative.honest_note: The only rung that is conservative in the everyday sense, and the only one whose universe is bias-free (6 broad ETFs — SPY/QQQ/IWM/TLT/GLD/DBC — so no survivorship haircut applies). It is also the most fold-consistent thing measured here: worst fold +0.49. You are giving up most of the return to get that: 5.6%/yr median versus 31.6% for balanced. kill_drawdown 0.35 sits well outside this strategy's worst measured anchor (-18.0%), so a normal drawdown will not trigger a permanent exit. NOTE ON ETFs: this rung is entirely ETFs (currently SPY/IWM/QQQ/DBC/GLD), and that is precisely why it is the only conservative option. Every stock-only alternative was measured and none goes below -28% drawdown — not low-vol ranking (-28.1%), not holding 12 names (-32.5%), not 20 names (-32.9%). On a long-only single-stock universe you are always fully exposed to the equity market; the bonds, gold and commodities are what break that. If you do not want an agent trading ETFs, the honest consequence is that this firm has one risk class, not four.
conservative.not_for: Anyone who wants the momentum book's returns. This is a different strategy, not a de-risked version of the same one.

balanced.headline: The incumbent. Concentrated stock momentum, six names.

measured.holdout: Sharpe 1.47, max drawdown -39% (2024-08 .. 2026-07, opened once — docs/TOURNAMENT_EQ.md)

balanced.honest_note: This is what has been running with real money since 2026-07-31, and the only rung with any out-of-sample evidence at all. That evidence is not flattering: -39% drawdown on the holdout, in a +37% bull market whose worst index drop was -19%. The -50% kill line is only 11pp below that. Sharpe after the mandatory survivorship haircut is 0.94, which is below the expected maximum of pure noise at the firm's registry size (~1.15) — the alpha claim did not pass the firm's own gate and is live only on an explicit owner override. Holds no ETFs: the defensive sleeve config was removed in v0.1.2 after measurement showed it allocated exactly 0.0 weight on every rebalance date (max ETF weight ever held: 0.0000). Removing it is bit-identical, so this rung is and always was 100% single-name stocks.
balanced.not_for: Anyone who would sell at -30%. That is inside normal behaviour for this book, not a malfunction.

aggressive.headline: Same strategy as balanced, concentrated into four names instead of six.

measured.holdout: not measured — the sealed holdout is deliberately not re-opened per profile

aggressive.honest_note: Four names instead of six. Median drawdown -32.9% against balanced's -30.9%, median CAGR 34.4% against 31.6% — a real but small difference that this data cannot distinguish from noise. Its worst measured anchor is -36.5%, which is close enough to the -50% halt that a bad sequence can end the book rather than ride through. We also tested three names: strictly worse on both axes (CAGR 37.8% at -31.1% drawdown on phase 0, and lower Sharpe), so the ladder stops at four rather than continuing. kill_drawdown is 0.55 here rather than balanced's 0.50: 1.5x this rung's worst measured anchor (-36.5%), per the headroom rule in docs/EQUITY.md. A tighter line on a more concentrated book buys nothing except a higher chance of a permanent exit during a survivable drawdown. Holds no ETFs — same as balanced, the dead defensive-sleeve config was removed in v0.1.2 with bit-identical results.
aggressive.not_for: Anyone expecting materially higher returns. The honest read is 'slightly more concentrated', not 'more aggressive' in any sense the data supports.

ultra_aggressive.headline: Two names. The most concentrated setting that is not simply worse than the one below it.

measured.holdout: not measured — the sealed holdout is deliberately not re-opened per profile

ultra_aggressive.honest_note: This is the only rung above 'aggressive' that actually buys something: median CAGR 39.7% against 34.4%, for a median drawdown of -36.4% against -32.9%. More return for more risk, which is what the word is supposed to mean. Everything more extreme was tested and rejected — see `rejected` below. Two names means one bad earnings report is roughly half the book, and the -48.6% worst anchor is why the halt line sits at -75%: at this concentration the kill switch is a backstop against a spiral, not protection of capital. If it trips you have lost three quarters of the account. Sharpe after the survivorship haircut is 0.85, the lowest of any rung and well under the ~1.15 noise ceiling — there is no evidence of skill here, only of leverage-by-concentration. Holds no ETFs — same as balanced, the dead defensive-sleeve config was removed in v0.1.2 with bit-identical results.
ultra_aggressive.not_for: Almost everyone. Losing half the account is a normal outcome at this setting, not a malfunction, and there is nothing in the strategy that will act to prevent it.

rejected.xsec_refined top_n=8 gate_mode=half: Drafted as the conservative rung on a phase-0 drawdown of -25.4%. Rejected: the anchor median is -29.2% (range -36.1% .. -19.6%), statistically indistinguishable from balanced, and it loses on every duration-aware measure — Ulcer index, average drawdown, time below -20%, recovery time (24 months vs 10 weeks for balanced), and 2022 return (-19.5% vs -5.4%). It bought a 2.7pp headline improvement, set by a single COVID observation, at the cost of 13pp of CAGR.
rejected.kill_drawdown 0.35 on a stock rung: Drafted for the conservative rung. Rejected: it sits inside the strategy family's own measured drawdown distribution (1 of 21 anchors already breaches it at -36.1%) and below its only out-of-sample drawdown (-39%), so it would convert a normal momentum drawdown into a permanent liquidating exit. This is the crypto-tournament lesson already recorded in config/equity_live.json.
rejected.max_single_name_frac 0.25 on a stock run: Rejected: the live planner enforces the cap and redistributes the excess (scripts/equity_rebalance.py), which would dismantle the defensive sleeve weighting that produced the measured figure — the published number would not describe the portfolio actually held.
rejected.xsec_refined top_n=1: Single name. CAGR 39.4% (LOWER than top_n=4's 41.2%) at a -50.9% drawdown, with a NEGATIVE out-of-sample fold (-0.342). Strictly worse than a less concentrated book on both axes — concentration past two names stops buying return and only buys variance.
rejected.xsec_refined top_n=3: CAGR 37.8% against top_n=4's 41.2% at a slightly worse drawdown. Dominated on both axes; the return/concentration curve is not monotone and 3 sits in a dip.
rejected.vol_scale=false variants: Removing the volatility scaling from the ranking does raise return (n=3: CAGR 41.3% median) but takes median drawdown to -43.1% and the worst anchor to -52.8%, which would need a halt line at -79%. At that point the kill switch no longer exists in any meaningful sense, and phase 0 printed a negative fold (-0.073). Rejected as beyond the point where a risk control can be said to be present.
rejected.faster rebalancing (every=10) and faster: Both lower return AND raise drawdown versus the shipped rungs — turnover cost eats the responsiveness. Not aggressive, just expensive.
